panels.description: Share of all cores busy, averaged over the scrape interval.

panels.title: GPU
panels.description: GPU active residency.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Memory in use as a share of installed memory.

panels.title: Thermal state
panels.description: macOS thermal pressure. Only Critical means heat is cutting the system's performance. Fair and Serious ask apps to cut back first.

panels.title: Power
panels.description: Whole-system power draw.

panels.title: SoC temperature
panels.description: Average SoC die temperature.

panels.title: Swap used
panels.description: Memory paged out to disk. Growth here means memory is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Download
panels.description: All interfaces, received.

panels.title: Upload
panels.description: All interfaces, sent.

panels.title: Disk read
panels.description: All disks.

panels.title: Disk write
panels.description: All disks.

panels.title: Utilization by resource
panels.description: The longest bar is the resource closest to its limit. Swap is its share of the swap currently allocated, which macOS grows on demand.

panels.title: Load, power and heat together
panels.description: Hover to line the series up in time: a CPU or GPU burst should show as power first, then heat, then fan speed.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: 100% is one core fully busy, as in Activity Monitor.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Resident memory of each app's processes. Memory shared between processes counts once for each of them.

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Received plus sent, on external interfaces.

panels.title: Disk
panels.description: Read plus written. Only processes running as you: macOS does not let other users read the counters of system daemons.

panels.title: GPU
panels.description: Share of GPU time.

panels.title: Energy
panels.description: macOS's own estimate of each app's power draw. Only processes running as you: macOS does not let other users read the counters of system daemons.

panels.title: CPU by app
panels.description: 100% is one core fully busy, as in Activity Monitor. The dashed line is all CPU time mactop measured, and the gap above the stack is mostly the kernel. Apps outside the 8 busiest over the time range are summed as Other.

panels.title: Memory by app
panels.description: Resident memory. Memory shared between processes counts once for each of them, so the stack is larger than the memory in use. Apps outside the 8 busiest over the time range are summed as Other.

panels.title: Network by app
panels.description: Received plus sent on external interfaces. Apps outside the 8 busiest over the time range are summed as Other.

panels.title: Disk by app
panels.description: Read plus written. The gap under the dashed line is system daemons. Only processes running as you: macOS does not let other users read the counters of system daemons. Apps outside the 8 busiest over the time range are summed as Other.

panels.title: GPU by app
panels.description: Share of GPU time, from each app's GPU clients. Apps outside the 8 busiest over the time range are summed as Other.

panels.title: Energy by app
panels.description: macOS's estimate of each app's power draw. It leaves out the display, the rest of the hardware and system daemons, which the Power chart above includes. Only processes running as you: macOS does not let other users read the counters of system daemons. Apps outside the 8 busiest over the time range are summed as Other.

panels.title: Processes now
panels.description: Every process of the app, with what it used over the last minute and what it holds now. A blank cell has no reading behind it. macOS does not let this user read the footprint, disk, power, wakeups, threads, files or sockets of other users' processes, and network stays blank for a process that has held no external connection since sysmon started. Pick the app in the menu at the top.

panels.title: CPU by process
panels.description: 100% is one core fully busy, as in Activity Monitor. Pick the app in the menu at the top.

panels.title: Resident memory by process
panels.description: Memory in RAM. Memory shared between processes counts once for each of them. Pick the app in the menu at the top.

panels.title: Footprint by process
panels.description: What Activity Monitor shows as Memory: what the process alone is responsible for, compressed and swapped memory included, shared memory left out. A line that only climbs points at a leak. Only processes running as you: macOS does not let other users read the counters of system daemons. Pick the app in the menu at the top.

panels.title: Network by process
panels.description: Received above the line, sent below it, on external interfaces. Pick the app in the menu at the top.

panels.title: Disk by process
panels.description: Read above the line, written below it. Only processes running as you: macOS does not let other users read the counters of system daemons. Pick the app in the menu at the top.

panels.title: GPU by process
panels.description: Share of GPU time. Pick the app in the menu at the top.

panels.title: Power by process
panels.description: macOS's estimate of each process's power draw. Only processes running as you: macOS does not let other users read the counters of system daemons. Pick the app in the menu at the top.

panels.title: Idle wakeups by process
panels.description: Times per second the process woke the CPU from idle. Frequent wakeups keep the chip out of its low-power states and cost battery even when CPU use looks low. Only processes running as you: macOS does not let other users read the counters of system daemons. Pick the app in the menu at the top.

panels.title: Page-ins by process
panels.description: Memory pages per second read in from disk because the process touched memory that was not in RAM, swapped out or in a mapped file. Steady page-ins while swap is in use mean the Mac is short of memory. Only processes running as you: macOS does not let other users read the counters of system daemons. Pick the app in the menu at the top.

panels.title: Threads by process
panels.description: A count that only climbs points at a thread leak. Only processes running as you: macOS does not let other users read the counters of system daemons. Pick the app in the menu at the top.

panels.title: Open files by process
panels.description: Files and directories held open. A count that only climbs points at a leaked file handle. Only processes running as you: macOS does not let other users read the counters of system daemons. Pick the app in the menu at the top.

panels.title: Sockets by process
panels.description: Network and local sockets held open. Many sockets with little traffic are idle connections kept open. Only processes running as you: macOS does not let other users read the counters of system daemons. Pick the app in the menu at the top.

panels.title: CPU usage
panels.description: Super cores are the M5's highest-clocked cores. Performance cores take the rest of the work.

panels.title: Cores now
panels.description: Each core's usage in the latest sample. Cores 0 to 11 are performance cores, 12 to 17 super cores.

panels.title: Cores over time
panels.description: One lane per core. Green is idle, red is saturated. A lane that stays red means one thread is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Power

targets.expr: (mactop_power_watts{component="total"} unless on() mactop_power_watts{component="system"} == 0) - ignoring(component) (mactop_power_watts{component="gpu"} unless on() mactop_power_watts{component="system"} == 0)

panels.description: mactop 2.1.5 reads CPU, DRAM and Neural Engine power as zero on this M5 Pro, so the SoC's share cannot be split further. Samples where those readings spike past the whole-machine reading are left out.

panels.title: Swap
panels.description: macOS allocates swap files as it needs them, so Allocated rising means memory ran short at that moment.

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Download above the line, upload below. Samples above 10 GB/s, faster than any link this Mac has, are mactop counter glitches and are left out.

panels.title: Disk throughput
panels.description: Read above the line, write below.

panels.title: Disk operations
panels.description: Many operations with little throughput means small random I/O.

panels.title: Hottest sensor by area
panels.description: The hottest of each area's sensors.

panels.title: Thermal state
panels.description: Any band other than green is time the Mac spent throttled.
